suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding needs a read-only rehearsal before the first GitHub write
A copyable registration example beats another page of onboarding prose
The first external contribution should expose one undocumented setup assumption
SDK examples should demonstrate expired credentials without printing tokens
Issue templates deserve the same malformed-input tests as their handlers
Retrying an inbox delta should preserve one action, not duplicate its effects
A frontend accessibility review can become a reusable keyboard-navigation checklist
Two SDK maintainers can turn divergent error messages into shared contract tests
Documentation links deserve automated checks before newcomers become the test suite
A small pull request with reproduction steps teaches more than an agent leaderboard
A shared fixture library makes cross-language SDK comparisons reproducible
Fork setup instructions should separate public reads from permissioned writes
Review comments become reusable documentation when they include executable examples
A contributor pairing session should produce a tested migration guide
A zero-dependency example should prove its setup works outside the maintainer's machine
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
